summary.title: Executive summary
summary.scope: Season 2026-27. Results verified through 2026-11-12 (174 games). Slate covered: 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-16 (31 games).

findings.title: The data reconciles exactly against the official NBA tables
findings.text: 348 team-games across 30 teams match the official games-played column with zero mismatch, and every team's wins and losses match the recomputed record. The slate of 31 games matches two independent official sources on date, time, teams and venue.

findings.title: The side model beats its baseline; the totals model does not
findings.text: Walk-forward over 114 out-of-sample games, the margin model cuts RMSE from 17.30 to 16.18 points and explains 12.5% of margin variance. The totals model lands at 20.35 against a 19.56 baseline and explains minus 8.2% of variance. Totals should not be traded on the strength of this model.

findings.title: No strategy survives its own validation gates
findings.text: 0 of 8 pass. The two strongest are fading our own totals of 235 or more (21 of 24, p = 0.0003) and backing road favourites of 8 or more (20 of 28, p = 0.0357). Both fail the minimum-sample gate of 100 and both are under-powered: S4b needs about 76 more games for 80% power. The honest reading is that the sample is too small, not that the effect is real or false.

findings.title: The measurable parlay correlation is small and the important ones are blank
findings.text: The correlation between our own spread residual and our own total residual is r = +0.091 with a 95% interval that contains zero, over 114 out-of-sample games. The joint cover-and-over rate is 0.246 against 0.219 under independence. Player-level correlations, the ones that decide same-game player-prop parlays, are blank because per-player game logs were never captured.

findings.title: Injuries are tracked line by line, and the minutes effect is quantified only where it can be
findings.text: 117 player rows from the newest official report, each with the printed status and reason. Where the player's season minutes per game are in the captured set, minutes at risk are computed from official minutes; where they are not, the cell is blank and says UNVERIFIED. No points impact is estimated anywhere.

findings.title: Home-court advantage is small and not established this season
findings.text: Least squares on 174 verified results gives +1.59 points with a two-sided p of 0.104 and 172 degrees of freedom. The fitted value is used because it is the least-squares estimate, but this sample does not establish the effect.

findings.title: Luck is measured, not assumed
findings.text: Every strategy is tested with an exact binomial test against its own null, a Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery correction, and a split-half direction check. A strategy has to survive all three plus a provenance check, a no-look-ahead check, a minimum-sample check and a power check. Nothing has survived all seven.

findings.title: A cross-engine comparison caught a sign-convention defect, not a modelling difference
findings.text: The two origination engines in this repository publish a spread field with the same name and opposite sign conventions: the origin engine stores a sportsbook-style line where a negative value means the home team is favoured, while the Edge Lab engine stores a projected home margin where a positive value means the home team is favoured. An earlier cut of this dashboard reported the two engines as picking different favourites in three games; that was an artefact of reading the raw fields, not a modelling difference. Normalised to one scale the engines agree on the favourite in all 17 games they share, with a median spread gap of 3.1 points and one gap above 10 points. The lesson is procedural rather than sporting: cross-engine numbers in this repository must be normalised before they are read, and that requirement is recorded as F-24.

bottom_line: The pipeline originates a defensible spread, total and fair moneyline for every one of the 31 games in the next three days, from official NBA inputs only.
It has not produced a strategy that passes its own gates, so nothing here should be traded as if it were an edge.
The largest available gain is not a better model but more games and a licensed price feed, plus a legal answer on whether NBA data may be used this way at all.
Every number on this site carries the source it was checked against, and every value that could not be confirmed is blank and listed on the Flagged for Review page.

flags.item: No licensed odds or price feed exists in this repository
flags.detail: Every published line is originated by this project. Nothing has been compared against a bookmaker's price, so no return-on-stake, no market edge and no de-vigged market probability can be computed.
flags.action: Decide whether a licensed feed is connected, or whether the project stays a paper/origination research system.

flags.item: NBA Terms of Use section 9 restricts gambling use of NBA Statistics and data
flags.detail: The model is built on nba.com statistics and official NBA injury reports. Commercial or wagering use of that data is restricted by the NBA's own terms.
flags.action: Obtain legal review before any public, commercial or wagering use. This dashboard is research output only.

flags.item: Dutch rules for offering online sports betting
flags.detail: Article 31a of the Betting and Gaming Act requires a Koa licence to offer online sports betting to residents of the Netherlands. Nothing in this repository constitutes a licensed offer.
flags.action: Legal review before publishing picks to end users. Owner decision required.

flags.item: No strategy passes every validation gate
flags.detail: 0 of 8 strategies pass all seven gates. The two strongest (S5 fade totals of 235+, S4b back road favourites of 8+) rest on 24 and 28 observations and are under-powered rather than disproven.
flags.action: Treat every strategy as a research candidate. Do not deploy on the strength of the leaderboard.

flags.item: Player-level correlations cannot be measured
flags.detail: Per-player game logs were never captured, so player points-vs-points, points-vs-rebounds and points-vs-assists correlations for same-game player props are left blank. They are the correlations that decide same-game player-prop parlays.
flags.action: Capture per-player game logs (nba.com/stats) to enable player-prop correlation work and SGP combo sizing.

flags.item: No injury report exists yet for the 11/15 and 11/16 games
flags.detail: The NBA index publishes reports only for games whose report window has opened. As of 2026-11-14 the newest report is the 11/13 07:30 PM file, which covers the 11/13 slate and the five 11/14 games. Availability for the 17 games on 11/15 and 11/16 is unknown and is left blank.
flags.action: Re-run the pipeline on each report release. Until then, availability for those games is blank by policy.

flags.item: Five team-games had not submitted a report at 07:30 PM on 11/13
flags.detail: New Orleans (vs DEN), Cleveland (vs DAL), Memphis (vs BKN), Chicago (vs MIN) and Miami (vs DET) show the printed status NOT YET SUBMITTED. No availability or minutes effect can be stated for them.
flags.action: Re-read those teams' rows from the next published report.

flags.item: Minutes-at-risk is only quantified for players inside the captured minutes set
flags.detail: Season minutes per game were captured for the top 31 players per team. A player outside that set has a blank minutes-at-risk cell and an explicit UNVERIFIED note, rather than an estimate.
flags.action: Widen the minutes capture to the full rotation of every team to remove the blanks.

flags.item: One injury reason string was split by a page break in the PDF extraction
flags.detail: Sacramento Kings forward Maxime Raynaud's reason reads 'Right Patella Sprain/Subluxation'; the extracted PDF text lost the middle segment 'rain/Subl' between chunks. The wording is corroborated by the 11/13 05:00 PM report ('Right Patella Subluxation').
flags.action: Re-check against the next published report to confirm the exact wording.

flags.item: The totals model is worse than its baseline
flags.detail: Walk-forward RMSE for the total is 20.35 against a 19.56 baseline (league-average total). The margin model improves on its baseline (16.18 vs 17.30). The totals side of the book is not usable.
flags.action: Rebuild the totals model, or restrict the system to sides until it beats baseline.

flags.item: Three snapshots of the same injury report are published in different trees
flags.detail: The /site/ tree carries the 11/13 05:00 PM report (117 rows, 18 of them unattributed); the origin engine's minutes-at-risk analysis used the 11/13 05:15 PM report; this dashboard carries the newer 11/13 07:30 PM report (117 player rows fully attributed plus 5 team rows). 12 statuses changed between 05:00 PM and 07:30 PM, and three team-games on 11/14 changed between 05:15 PM and 07:30 PM.
flags.action: Owner picks one snapshot per slate and the other trees are regenerated or retired. This dashboard uses the newest report.

flags.item: Seven parallel site trees with different identifier namespaces
flags.detail: /, /docs/, /site/, /lab/, /research/, /edge/ and /origin/ were produced by seven sequential sessions and use incompatible ID namespaces (7C-F-xx, F-xx, F01-xx, IR-xx, Q-xx, S1x, S0x, ...). The same subject can carry different numbers in different trees.
flags.action: This dashboard is the consolidation; decide whether to retire the older trees to avoid conflicting numbers.

flags.item: requirements.txt pins a dependency that nothing imports
flags.detail: requirements.txt lists requests==2.31.0, but every generator in the repository is standard-library only (Python 3.11+).
flags.action: Delete the pin or document why it is kept.

flags.item: No LICENSE file
flags.detail: The repository has no licence, so reuse rights are undefined for a project that publishes derived NBA statistics.
flags.action: Add a licence, or keep the repository private.

flags.item: The official schedule PDF is marked subject to change
flags.detail: The PDF header reads 'AS OF AUGUST 13, 2026 | SUBJECT TO CHANGE'. Dates, times and the game numbering can still move.
flags.action: Re-verify the slate from nba.com/schedule before acting on any date beyond today.

flags.item: The schedule PDF marker column has no published legend
flags.detail: Rows carry markers such as C and R whose meaning is not documented in the PDF. C matches the NBA Cup games confirmed on nba.com/schedule; R could not be confirmed.
flags.action: Ask the NBA or leave the marker unexplained.

flags.item: The official NBA CDN schedule JSON returns HTTP 500
flags.detail: https://cdn.nba.com/static/json/staticData/scheduleLeagueV2_1.json could not be fetched from this environment, so the machine-readable official game list was unavailable.
flags.action: Retry from a normal network; it would give game IDs and home/away in one call.

flags.item: Official team statistics move during the season
flags.detail: The 30-team table in this dashboard was read at 2026-11-14 while two 11/13 games were still in progress, so it is a season-to-date snapshot, not a fixed constant.
flags.action: Re-fetch before every publication; every row carries the retrieval date.

flags.item: Game results are sourced from a secondary site, not from the NBA
flags.detail: The 174-game training log behind the model was assembled from Basketball-Reference result pages. Basketball-Reference is a trusted secondary source but is not the NBA. The aggregate check against the official GP column reconciles exactly, which is the strongest statement available.
flags.action: Re-source results from nba.com box scores, or document the reliance.

flags.item: Market-price picks in an older tree are tier C and paper only
flags.detail: data/picks.json (served by /site/) publishes picks with positive expected value against an ESPN odds feed. Those picks are labelled 'TIER C - pre-validation, paper only', they carry the same licensing flags as F-02 and F-03, and no strategy behind them has passed the gates.
flags.action: Owner decides whether that page stays public. This dashboard publishes only originated prices.

flags.item: No bankroll, staking or ruin policy is defined
flags.detail: Nothing in the repository defines stake sizing, bankroll, drawdown limits or when to stop a strategy.
flags.action: Define the policy before any strategy is traded, even on paper.

flags.item: The three-day window is hard coded
flags.detail: The picks generator targets 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16 as literals, so it does not roll forward on its own as new games arrive.
flags.action: Derive the window from the official schedule at run time.

flags.item: A worked example of the PDF page-break loss is published as a transcription
flags.detail: One reason string in the injury table is a reconstruction rather than a literal copy. It is marked in the row itself so a reviewer can see exactly which cell was reconstructed.
flags.action: Confirm against the next published report.

flags.item: The repository's two origination engines publish the same spread field with opposite sign conventions
flags.detail: The origin engine (model/build.py) stores a sportsbook-style line in orig_spread_home, where a negative value means the home team is favoured; the Edge Lab engine (pipeline/run_model.py) stores a projected home margin in origin_spread_home, where a positive value means the home team is favoured. The two field names are almost identical and the conventions are opposite, so any code that compares them without normalising first reads a large spurious disagreement. This was found in this session: an early version of the hub dashboard reported the engines as picking different favourites in three games, which was an artefact of this sign error, not a modelling difference. After normalising both to a single home-margin scale the two engines agree on the favourite in all 17 games they share, with a median spread gap of 3.1 points and one gap above 10 points (CHI at MIN, 11.8). Note also that the origin engine publishes 174 games while the Edge Lab engine publishes a different number of rows, so their overlap is only 17 games.
flags.action: Normalise the sign convention in every comparison, store the convention next to the value, and keep the agreement metric published on the Lines page. Until the field names or the conventions are unified, treat any cross-engine number as unsafe to compare by eye.

questions.next_step: Owner decides: connect a licensed feed, or keep the system research-only and publish fair prices with no expected value.

questions.question: How many games does a strategy need before it can be called skill?
questions.known: Seven gates are defined. The two strongest signals rest on 24 and 28 observations (21/24 and 20/28). The minimum-sample gate of 100 is not met, and the observed effects are under-powered: S4b needs about 76 more games to reach 80% power.
questions.missing: More seasons of data, and an agreed minimum observation count for a promoted strategy.
questions.next_step: Re-run the same gates after roughly 100 further games and publish the power calculation for each strategy.

questions.question: Can the totals side of the book be used at all?
questions.known: Walk-forward RMSE for the total is 20.35 against a 19.56 league-average baseline, so the totals model is worse than doing nothing. The margin model improves on its baseline (16.18 vs 17.30).
questions.missing: A totals model that beats the baseline.
questions.next_step: Rebuild the totals model on possession and pace inputs, then re-run the same walk-forward test.

questions.question: What is the real home-court advantage in 2026-27?
questions.known: Least squares on 174 verified results gives +1.59 points with a two-sided p of 0.104 and 172 degrees of freedom, so this sample does not establish it.
questions.missing: A season-long estimate, and a decision on whether to use the fitted value or a published prior.
questions.next_step: Recompute after the season sample grows and compare with the league's own home record.

questions.question: Which injuries actually move the line, and by how much?
questions.known: 117 player rows are available from the official report, and minutes-at-risk is quantified where the player's season minutes per game are in the captured top-31 set. Six players are quantified with their official minutes; the rest are blank.
questions.missing: Per-player game logs, a replacement-player model, and the elasticity of team rating to minutes. The current impact is a minutes count, not a points estimate.
questions.next_step: Capture per-player box scores and fit a minutes-to-rating model; until then no points impact is published.

questions.question: How correlated are player props in the same game?
questions.known: Team-level and game-level correlations are measured (home points vs away points r = 0.128, n = 174; spread residual vs total residual r = 0.091, n = 114; cover-and-over phi = 0.109, n = 114). Player-level correlations are blank.
questions.missing: Per-player game logs, which were never captured.
questions.next_step: Pull nba.com/stats player box scores for two seasons and compute the same-game player correlation matrix with confidence intervals.

questions.question: Are the player-prop lines published here real lines or projections?
questions.known: The prop table carries official season averages and a pro-rata minutes redistribution assumption. It explicitly states the over/under distribution is not established and marks every line as unverified.
questions.missing: A verified prop line feed and a projected-minutes model.
questions.next_step: Owner decides whether to keep publishing projections with the caveat, or to suppress the prop page until a real feed exists.

questions.question: Which injury report should be canonical when two versions of the same report exist?
questions.known: The 11/13 07:30 PM report (used here, 117 player rows fully attributed) and the 11/13 05:00 PM report (used by the /site/ tree, 18 rows unattributed) disagree on 12 statuses.
questions.missing: A rule that says which snapshot is authoritative and that every tree obeys it.
questions.next_step: Owner names one snapshot per slate and the older trees are either regenerated or retired.

questions.question: Are the 174 results in the training log correct?
questions.status: answered for the aggregate, open per game
questions.known: 348 team-games reconcile exactly against the official games-played column for all 30 teams (mismatch 0), and the official W-L columns match the recomputed records. 81 of the overlapping injury rows also match the earlier independent transcription.
questions.missing: A per-game check of all 174 results against official box scores.
questions.next_step: Pull nba.com box scores for the 174 games and diff every score line.

questions.question: How are the seven existing site trees related, and which one is authoritative?
questions.known: Seven trees exist with incompatible ID namespaces and partly different data snapshots. This dashboard consolidates them and states which artifact each number comes from.
questions.missing: A decision to retire the older trees, keep them as archives, or keep them live.
questions.next_step: Owner decides; then this dashboard becomes the only live tree and the others are archived.

questions.question: What is the stake plan and the stop rule?
questions.known: Nothing in the repository defines stake sizing, bankroll, drawdown limits or a stop rule.
questions.next_step: Owner sets a bankroll and a flat or fractional stake rule before any strategy is traded on paper.

questions.question: Can the system roll forward to the next slate without a manual run?
questions.known: The picks generator hard codes 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16, so it does not advance by itself.
questions.missing: A scheduler and a window that is derived from the official schedule.
questions.next_step: Derive the window from the official schedule at run time and add a scheduled job.

questions.question: Is the model's edge skill or luck?
questions.known: Margin variance explained is 12.5% and total variance explained is -8.2%. The two best strategies pass the raw-p and false-discovery gates but fail on sample size. That is the signature of an under-powered result, not a demonstrated edge.
questions.missing: A larger sample and a pre-registered strategy list so that the surviving strategy is not one of many that were tried.
questions.next_step: Freeze the strategy list now, then re-test the frozen list after 100 further games.

questions.question: What would the picks be worth at a real price?
questions.known: The project publishes fair moneylines derived from its own model probabilities for every game in the window.
questions.missing: Any market price to compare them with, so expected value, edge and hold-adjusted numbers stay blank.
questions.next_step: Same as Q-02: a licensed odds feed, or a decision to publish fair prices only.

questions.question: Is the three-day window the right horizon?
questions.known: The brief sets a maximum of three days ahead and the system covers 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-16 (31 games).
questions.missing: A decision on whether the horizon should shrink as report coverage improves, since injury reports for 11/15 and 11/16 do not exist yet.
questions.next_step: Owner confirms the horizon; the generator should then derive it from the schedule.

suggestions.suggestion: Retire the six older site trees and keep this dashboard as the single live surface
suggestions.why: Seven trees carry the same subjects with different numbers and incompatible ID namespaces. A reviewer cannot tell which figure is current without reading the coordination log.
suggestions.options: A - keep all seven and mark them 'archived' at the top of each page; B - keep /origin/ (the engine) plus this dashboard and delete the rest; C - keep only this dashboard
suggestions.impact: High - removes the risk of acting on a stale number.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a single 'eligible to act' flag at the top of every pick row
suggestions.why: Every pick currently carries its own strategy status string in prose. One machine-readable flag makes the leaderboard and the picks consistent.
suggestions.options: A - one flag with the gate list that failed; B - three states (eligible, provisional, not eligible)
suggestions.impact: High - removes ambiguity in the picks table.

suggestions.suggestion: Publish the gate score and the power calculation for every strategy, not just a pass or fail
suggestions.why: S5 and S4b fail only on sample size. Showing the power curve tells a reviewer whether to wait or to abandon a strategy.
suggestions.options: A - power curve per strategy; B - the number of extra games needed at the current effect size
suggestions.impact: Medium - turns a null result into a decision.

suggestions.suggestion: Capture per-player game logs for two seasons
suggestions.why: Player-level correlation is the missing input for player-prop parlays and for any real injury-to-minutes impact. Four correlation cells are blank because of it.
suggestions.options: A - nba.com/stats player box scores; B - skip player props entirely and remove those pages
suggestions.impact: High - unlocks the whole player-prop branch.

suggestions.suggestion: Re-source the game results from nba.com box scores
suggestions.why: Results currently come from Basketball-Reference. The aggregate check reconciles exactly, but a per-game check against official box scores is stronger.
suggestions.options: A - replace the results log with nba.com box scores; B - keep Basketball-Reference and keep the provenance note
suggestions.impact: Medium - makes every model input official.

suggestions.suggestion: Derive the three-day window from the official schedule instead of hard coding it
suggestions.why: The current generator only knows 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16, so it will produce an empty or wrong slate tomorrow.
suggestions.options: A - read nba.com/schedule at run time; B - read the official schedule PDF; C - keep it manual but document the update step
suggestions.impact: High - the system becomes usable on an ongoing basis.

suggestions.suggestion: Run a scheduled check that every published number still matches its source
suggestions.why: Official statistics move during the season, and an injury report is replaced eight times a day. Numbers on a static site decay silently.
suggestions.options: A - a daily job that re-fetches and diffs; B - a printed retrieval timestamp on every table (already partly done)
suggestions.impact: Medium - stops the site from quietly going stale.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a 'last updated' banner and a per-table retrieval stamp
suggestions.why: A reader cannot tell whether a number was published today or three weeks ago.
suggestions.options: A - banner only; B - banner plus a stamp on every table

suggestions.suggestion: Add a filter box to the picks and injuries tables
suggestions.why: Both tables are long and the useful view is usually one date or one team.
suggestions.options: A - plain client-side filter with no framework; B - one filter per column

suggestions.suggestion: Add a bankroll and staking panel next to the leaderboard
suggestions.why: A leaderboard without a stake rule invites the reader to size bets by confidence rather than by risk.
suggestions.options: A - flat 1 unit per bet with a stated bankroll; B - fractional Kelly with a published cap
suggestions.impact: Medium - prevents the most common misuse of a leaderboard.

suggestions.options: A - delete both; B - keep them but rename to tools/ and mark them clearly
